summary: A short note from Alex McKenzie at BBN that attaches network traffic statistics for the ARPANET for October 1972. The tables show how many packets each host sent over the period. They cover the whole month, the four days before the ICCC and the three days of the ICCC. BBN had been giving these figures to ARPA each month and now shared them with the whole network community.

plainLanguage.summary: This is a monthly tally from the early internet, showing how many packets each computer sent. Think of counting how many letters each house mailed in a month, so the post office can see where the traffic is.

questions: how much traffic did each arpanet host send
how many packets did the arpanet carry in 1972
subtitle: Packet counts for every ARPANET host in October 1972, plus the ICCC tryout and demonstration days.

tldr.problem: Network traffic figures were gathered each month, and the wider community had no view of them.
tldr.mechanism: The note attaches three Host Throughput Summary tables listing packets output per host, split into internode and intranode, with daily averages.
tldr.outcome: October 1972 totalled 40711450 internode and 13589160 intranode packets. The note updates RFC 400.

today: RFC 413 updates RFC 400, and the next monthly note, RFC 422, updates it in turn. It is a historical snapshot of early ARPANET traffic.

sections.title: What Is Attached
sections.content: A. McKenzie of BBN attaches three sets of network traffic statistics: the entire month of October 1972, the four days preceding the ICCC (October 20 to 23, labelled the ICCC tryout) and the three days of the ICCC (October 24 to 26). The note updates RFC 400.
sections.plainLanguage: Three scoreboards: the whole month, the practice days and the big show days.

sections.title: How the Tables Are Laid Out
sections.content:
Each table is a Host Throughput Summary of packets output. Rows are hosts such as UCLA, SRI, UCSB, UTAH, BBN, MIT and ISI. Columns give internode packets, intranode packets, the total, the average daily internode figure and the number of days counted.

Sites with several hosts show a subtotal line. TINK and BELV are listed as having no traffic. The October table notes missing data for 4 days.
sections.plainLanguage: Every computer gets a row with how many packets it sent out, and how many days were counted.

sections.title: The Totals
sections.content:
For all of October 1972 the totals are 40711450 internode and 13589160 intranode packets, a daily average of 1357048 and 452972, with an internode packets-to-messages ratio of 1.07.

The ICCC tryout days total 8654547 internode and 1577098 intranode packets (ratio 1.13). The three ICCC days total 8437328 internode and 895413 intranode packets (ratio 1.05).
sections.plainLanguage: Add up all the rows and you get how busy the whole network was, and the practice and show days can be compared with the month.

references.text: RFC 400, the earlier traffic statistics note this one updates.
